text.p: Chile's Embotelladora Andina SA said its stock and American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) would split Monday.
The bottler said in an April 1 statement local shareholders would get one Series A and one Series B share for each common share held.
For each ADR held, one ADR Series A and one ADR Series B will be given, each representing six shares of their respective series.

With the split carried out, Andina will have 395.6 million Series A shares and 395.6 million Series B shares issued. Of those, a total of 380.1 million shares of each series will be outstanding, and 15.5 million of each series will be held by the company as treasury stock.
Series A shares will have full voting rights. Series B will have limited voting rights, and holders will have the right to get any dividends distributed for Series A shares with an extra 10 percent.
Andina's ADRs closed on Friday at 38.
